title: Female Bank Rehabilitation Support Worker
description:
Female Bank Rehabilitation Support Worker

Location: Barrow, Cumbria

Salary: £16.00 - £18.00 per hour

Vacancy Type: Permanent

Are you looking interested in enabling the ongoing rehabilitation of a lady based near Kendal? If you are seeking a position which offers you flexibility around your working hours but where you can make a significant impact on the rehabilitation and quality of life to our client, this is the perfect role for you.

The Client

Hannah is a lady in her 30 s who suffered a brain injury in 2020 which has left her with a significant visual impairment, compromised coordination in both fine and gross motor skills and increased fatigue. Hannah needs some occasional help with hands-on personal care although help is generally required in a supportive capacity in this area. Hannah lives at home with her husband and their dog who is very much one of the family . She is a bubbly lady with a great sense of humour, enjoying banter with those close to her and has a naturally gregarious and mischievous personality. Candidates will need to have a natural sense of fun and zest for life to keep up with Hannah s enthusiasm for living life to the full. Hannah requires support in every area of her activities of daily living including; personal care, domestic organisation (washing/cleaning/cooking), mealtimes, mobilising safely, driving, scheduling her timetable and activities, using electronic devices and caring for her dog.

Hobbies & Interests

Hannah likes to be busy and enjoys being out and about in the community accessing leisure and recreational facilities, going shopping, for coffee with friends and spending time with her family, especially her young daughter. Hannah likes to present herself well; she has a particular interest in fashion and likes to have her nails manicured and painted regularly. She likes to make sure her home is cosy and comfortable. Hannah also loves to go out in the evenings to bowling or bingo, going for day s out as well as enjoying short breaks and holidays within the UK and abroad. Candidates must hold a full, clean, manual driving licence and be happy to drive Hannah s vehicle. Hannah is very easily influenced by the opinions and thoughts of others and can suffer from low mood, therefore, it is the expectation that candidates always uphold their professional boundaries and positive reinforcement strategies whilst working with her.

Candidates should have the following skills:
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal;
- Motivational skills in creating a positive atmosphere when Hannah has low mood;
- Be an creative thinker able to identify new recreational and leisure interests, which are suitable and appropriate with the ability to fully risk assess these;
- Experience of working with clients with sustained brain injury would be helpful, although full training will be given;
- Experience in working in a family home would be an advantage;
- Full, clean, manual UK driving licence and be happy to drive the Client s vehicle;
- Flexibility to accompany Hannah on short breaks and holidays;
- Ability to build relationships with the family and MDT, whilst maintaining professional boundaries;
- Willingness to assist with personal care.

The Role

The Support Worker role with Hannah is based within her home and involves encouraging and enabling her to fulfil her hobbies and interests whilst adhering to the care plan and implementing the therapy programmes.

We require Female Bank Rehabilitation Support Worker(s) to join the existing care team with the purpose of actively encouraging Hannah to engage in her therapy programmes to help her achieve her goals, increase her independence and take on stronger maternal responsibilities, as a mother to her daughter.

Bank Rehabilitation Support Workers

We are looking for Bank Rehabilitation Support Worker(s) who are able to offer the flexibility to pick up shifts when offered. There are no guaranteed hours however the successful candidates will be required to undertake shifts which may be up to 24 hours in length to include sleeping night shift hours.

Rates of Pay

Hands-On Hours (07 00)

Monday to Friday: £16.00 per hour

Saturday & Sunday: £18.00 per hour

Sleeping Night (23 00)

Monday to Sunday: Prevailing National Minimum Wage (currently £12.71 per hour)

If you are interested in a position with Hannah and feel you have the skills, experience, enthusiasm and sense of adventure to provide support to her, please submit your CV in the first instance with a note of the hours of work you are interested in each week.

Exemption is claimed under the Equality Act 2010 Part 1 Schedule 9.

To Apply

If you are excited at the prospective of joining this established care team providing care and support to Hannah, please submit your CV.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

Location: Ulverston, Cumbria
Salary: £24,479 per annum pro rata
Contract: Permanent (Requires a full DBS)
Hours Per Week: 31.5hours

Advertising End Date: We reserve the right to withdraw this vacancy when we feel we have enough suitable candidates

Benefits - We Are Offering:

As well as knowing that what we do is making a positive difference to people s lives, you will receive fair pay and have access to a wide range of rewards and benefits as one of our employees.
- 28 days holiday (including bank holidays) increasing with long service.
- Pension contributions into NEST Scheme on a salary sacrifice basis meaning NI savings
- £500 onboarding payment (paid on completion of 6 months probationary period)
- Private Health Care scheme funded by Oaklea.
- Free access to round the clock employee assistance program for advice and support
- Length of Service Awards
- Access to foundation and bespoke training and development

About Us:

At Oaklea we work in partnership with the individuals we support (our customers). We strive to support people within the framework of the seven keys to Citizenship; Love, Freedom, Life, Purpose, Help, Money and Home.

Every employee wants a purposeful job - to do something meaningful. At Oaklea, we can give you that. You will have opportunities to develop as a person, colleague, leader and advocate. You ll make new friends and feel inspired to reach your potential. We will ask a lot of you - but you ll get back so much more. With us, it is never just a job .

In return for your hard work and passion, we can give you real meaning and purpose in your work.

About the Role:

As a Lifestyle Co-ordinator, you will work as part of a dedicated team to provide person-centred support to the five gentlemen living in the home.

Every person is different, and your role will be about getting to know each individual their personality, preferences, interests, routines and aspirations and supporting them to have choice and control over their lives.

You will help the gentlemen to enjoy activities they love, access their local community, develop their skills and try new experiences.

Your role will include:
- Supporting individuals with their personal care and daily routines.
- Supporting with medication in line with individual care plans and training.
- Developing positive, trusting relationships with the people we support.
- Understanding and responding to different communication styles and individual ways of expressing choices, needs and emotions.
- Supporting people who communicate without verbal speech to express themselves and make choices.
- Helping individuals to access the local community and take part in activities they enjoy.
- Supporting people to develop and maintain their independence and life skills.
- Encouraging people to try new experiences and take positive risks.
- Supporting individuals to work towards their personal goals and aspirations.
- Helping with appointments, shopping, budgeting, cooking and domestic tasks where required.
- Promoting health and wellbeing.
- Supporting people to maintain relationships and connections that are important to them.
- Working alongside colleagues, families and other professionals to provide consistent, person-centred support.
- Completing appropriate records and documentation to ensure high standards of care and support.

The home is a welcoming environment where the people we support are encouraged to be active participants in their own lives. You will help create opportunities for them to enjoy their interests, make choices, develop their confidence and be part of their local community.

What we need from you:

You don't necessarily need previous experience of working in care. What matters most to us is your attitude, values and commitment to making a positive difference.

We are looking for someone who is:
- Kind, caring and compassionate.
- Patient, reliable and approachable.
- Positive, enthusiastic and willing to get involved.
- A good communicator who can build meaningful relationships.
- Respectful of people's choices, rights and individuality.
- Patient and observant, with an interest in understanding how each person communicates.
- Comfortable working as part of a team.
- Willing to learn and develop new skills.
- Able to encourage and motivate others while promoting their independence.
- Flexible and able to respond positively to the changing needs.

Experience of supporting people with learning disabilities, autism or complex communication needs would be beneficial, but full training and support will be provided.

Most importantly, we are looking for someone who sees the person first and is committed to helping the gentlemen we support live the lives they choose.

Working pattern

This is a 31.5-hour permanent position based at our registered care home in Ulverston.

The role involves working as part of a rota, which may include days, evenings, weekends and bank holidays, depending on the needs of the people we support.

Sleep-in shifts are part of the role where required.

A full DBS check will be required for this role.

Driving licence is preferred but not essential.

An Enhanced DBS will be required for each successful candidate (Paid for by Oaklea, T&Cs apply)

Your Privacy Matters

We ll use the information you share with us only for recruitment purposes, in line with the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Your details will be stored securely and kept only as long as needed.

Click on APPLY today forwarding a recent copy of your CV and cover letter for consideration in the first instance.

No agencies please
